The May 1, 2019 FOMC statement is mildly dovish/constructive (patience on rates with inflation below 2% and a strong labor market). However, the April 2019 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey points to tightening credit supply and softer demand: banks tightened standards for C&I and construction/land development loans and tightened other terms across bank sizes; they reported weaker demand for HELOCs, credit cards, and other consumer loans, with demand roughly unchanged for auto and subprime mortgages; foreign banks reported similar patterns and concerns about loan quality. These SLOOS findings align with the statement’s noted cooling in household spending and business investment, reinforcing a cautious stance and tempering the positive tilt. Net: shift from slightly positive to near-neutral/cautious-positive.
